metadata.title: Pass 3 reference table: centrifugal (directional) quench front and explicit 3-stage single-domain hierarchy for Coscinodiscus wailesii biosilica
metadata.provenance_note: Literature values below were transcribed offline from the cited papers / from the Pass 1-2 reference JSON; the two new DOIs (furukawa1992, schmid1983) were NOT re-verified online during Pass 3 (network tools disabled). Model-regime values marked model_prediction are outputs of this script's own model and are NOT empirical.

sources.citation: Furukawa H (1992). Phase separation by directional quenching and morphological transition. Physica A 180(1-2):128-155.
Schmid A-MM, Volcani BE (1983). Wall morphogenesis in Coscinodiscus wailesii Gran and Angst. I. Valve morphology and development of its architecture. Journal of Phycology 19(4):387-402.
Sumper M (2002). A phase separation model for the nanopatterning of diatom biosilica. Science 295(5564):2430-2433.

centrifugal_directional_quench_model.governing_pde: d(phi)/dt = M * laplacian(phi^3 - a(r,t) * phi - epsilon^2 * laplacian(phi))
centrifugal_directional_quench_model.quench_field: a(r,t) = tanh((R(t) - r) / w),  R(t) = R0 + v_front * t
centrifugal_directional_quench_model.solidification_front: R_s(t) = R(t) - lag;  pixels with r < R_s(t) are frozen (zero mobility); leaked mass is re-projected uniformly onto mobile pixels
centrifugal_directional_quench_model.biological_mapping: Coscinodiscus valve silicification proceeds centrifugally from the central annulus/pattern centre towards the margin (Schmid & Volcani 1983); the lagging solidification represents silica condensation around the LCPA phase (Sumper 2002)
centrifugal_directional_quench_model.dimensionless_front_speed: Pe = v_front / (lambda_c * sigma_max),  lambda_c = 2 pi sqrt(2) eps / sqrt(1 - 3 phi0^2),  sigma_max = M (1 - 3 phi0^2)^2 / (4 eps^2)

front_velocity_ablation.regime_source: Furukawa (1992) directional-quench morphological transition (front-perpendicular lamellae at slow front speed, front-parallel at faster speed, isotropic spinodal pattern as v -> infinity); the exact crossover speed here is a model_prediction of this script, not a literature value
front_velocity_ablation.isotropic_null: same disc, a = +1 everywhere from t = 0, no front, no freezing, mean of 3 seeds

anisotropy_metric.definition: A = < |d_theta phi|^2 - |d_r phi|^2 > / < |d_theta phi|^2 + |d_r phi|^2 > in the margin annulus 0.6 R_max <= r < R_max

centrifugal_directional_quench_model.specimen_gap: The vendored SEM (coscinodiscus_diatom_specimen.jpg) shows the valve face at three magnifications but NOT the valve margin; no direct empirical value of A exists in this dataset (Pass 4: vendor a Coscinodiscus wailesii valve-margin / costae SEM).

tiers.confinement: tier-1 silica walls frozen; chambers = tier-1 pores eroded 3 px
tier-2 silica frozen; chambers = tier-2 pores eroded 1 px

three_stage_single_domain_model.epsilon_rule: eps_k = a_k_px * sqrt(1 - 3 phi0_k^2) / (2 pi sqrt 2)  (fastest-growing spinodal wavelength set equal to the Sumper tier pitch)
three_stage_single_domain_model.scale_invariance: x -> L x, eps -> L eps, t -> L^2 t leaves the Cahn-Hilliard equation invariant; dt_tiers scale accordingly

cribrella_per_cribrum_pore.source: Sumper (2002) centered-hexagonal H(1) = 7; reference JSON tier 3 subpores_per_parent

cribrum_per_foramen.source: reference JSON tier 2 subpores_per_parent (Sumper 2002 Figs. 1-3, 7-19 range)

three_stage_single_domain_model.resolution_limit_note: d_3 = 42 nm is 3.4 px at 12.5 nm/px — at the grid floor (components >= 6 px are counted); the 512^2 domain holds ~12 foramina. A 1024^2 (or larger) grid is needed to resolve cribrella with >= 8 px diameters.
